messages.content: Write a job posting for a senior backend engineer at a mid-sized fintech company. Around 250 words.

**Senior Backend Engineer**
Remote (US) or Chicago office · $180k–$215k + equity

We handle money movement for roughly 40,000 small businesses. Payroll clears, invoices settle, ACH files leave on a schedule that has no interest in whether our on-call engineer is having a rough week. The backend team is nine people. We want a tenth.

The work: our ledger service and the payment orchestration layer wrapped around it. Go and Postgres, plus an aging Python service still doing reconciliation that somebody will need to kill off eventually. Things we shipped lately: settlement latency down from 90 seconds to under 10, and a rewrite of our idempotency handling after a bad week in March showed us where we'd been wrong.

We're after about six years of backend work, some of it on systems where getting the answer right mattered more than getting it fast. Payments background is a plus, not a requirement; folks coming from billing, inventory, or anything double-entry usually get up to speed fast. You should want to own a service from end to end, pager included.

Straight talk about the downsides: we're regulated, which means compliance work, and audit season is a slog. Our test suite runs 14 minutes. The reconciliation path carries debt we're chipping away at steadily instead of all at once.

The upsides: small team, actual ownership, nobody standing between you and a deploy. We ship most days. Reviews are careful without being personal.

The process: a screen, a systems design conversation, a paid take-home, and a team chat. Four to five hours across two weeks.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
